newsitem.title: IRAQ: Jordan's king calls Iraq's Saddam on Eid al-Fitr.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's king calls Iraq's Saddam on Eid al-Fitr.

text.p: King Hussein of Jordan telephoned Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on Saturday to offer "fraternal blessings" on the Moslem feast of Eid al-Fitr, the official Iraqi News Agency said.

The call was the first reported contact between the leaders since the king distanced himself from Saddam by openly calling for a change of government in Baghdad after sheltering senior defectors in 1995.

"INA has learned that His Majesty King Hussein of Jordan contacted President Saddam Hussein this morning expressing his fraternal congratulations, blessings and wishes for a profusion of health for his excellency's prosperity and progress for the sisterly Iraqi people," INA said.
Recently senior Jordanian officials have been sending conciliatory gestures towards Baghdad, Jordan's largest trade partner.
"The president expressed to King Hussein his fraternal appreciation and wishes and reciprocated congratulations and blessings," INA said.

Iraq supplies Jordan with all its oil needs and Saddam last month agreed to increase sales by seven percent for 1997. Jordan imported about 75,000 barrels per day of crude and refined products in 1996.
